Dear participants of the Waterford co-design workshops^[6 and 7 October], 

Thank you for your inputs at the co-design workshops this week. There was a lot to take in from all of your comments.  We will be looking closely at the materials developed in the workshop over the next weeks and months, with an aim to using your insights to improve the trial and better understand how shared electric mobility hubs might succeed here in Ireland or elsewhere.  

# Initial takeaways 

My initial takeaways from your comments are: 

- there are challenges in using the apps and other aspects of the user interface^[Including for *new users*, for whom separate step-by-step instructions for the e-cars and the e-bikes in multiple formats (especially on-site signage) might help. However, the need to *both plug in and ALSO activate* the car charging with the access card is also an issue - not necessarily obvious to all users who might be expecting plugging in the cars would be enough to start recharging.];
- reliability and availability may be limiting the potential of the hub^[Especially with respect to the cars' batteries running down when plugged in but *not* charging.], but might be improved on with more local involvement in the day-to-day management^[Potential for local shops, community members or others to be involved in regularly monitoring the vehicles, taking them for a spin around the block every few days, acting as an immediate contact to help users etc. perhaps in exchange for a reduced rate, free hours, (in the case of shops) free use of cargo bikes for short deliveries / dropping off purchases just made in store, etc. .];
- topography is an important factor for the use of the e-bikes, given the location of the hub at the top of a hill^[Need to walk up the hill to get to the hub, e-bikes not necessarily having the power or sufficient remaining charge to get up hills (when returning to the hub), braking while going downhill (especially for first-time riders).] 
- there may be potential to provide weather protected and well sheltered seating, as there is not much other than the bandstand nearby (and that just has steps).
- there may be potential for a bit of friendly competition between Waterford and the other hubs as far as tracking a leaderboard of 'most trips', 'most carbon saved' or something similar. 
- there may be potential for alternate vehicle types, given the demographics (i.e. older population)^[Electric tricycle? Tandem bike?] and other characteristics of the surrounding area (i.e. more apartment living and interest in car-free life^[Potential for e-cars, e-vans, additional e-cargobikes], common use of walking and cycling^[Many people already have their own bikes so shorter-range e-bikes may be less useful, but might be useful to have longer range e-bikes for longer trips.]  )

# Immediate steps


## Pop-ups (seating?)


```{r legitimisation, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE, fig.margin = TRUE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="QR code for short 2-pager with details about pop-ups and otherwise legitimising implementation"}

knitr::include_graphics("graphics/nine_strategies_for_legitimising_implementation.jpeg")

```

There may be opportunities in the short term to provide additional seating.  
This might be experimented with through adopting a pop-up^[See also https://james-reynolds.github.io/implementation_transit_priority_handout.html (QR code above).] approach,
to see what might work and what the community might like to have. Or even if they want to have anything at all^[Pop-downs are always possible.]. Watch out for that (possibly) happening sometime soon near the hub!

\newthought{A great thing about co-design research is that *everyone* can take part} in improving the output if they would like too! If you are interested in having a go and making your own videos or other forms of information about the hub please feel free to just go ahead. Drop us a line if you'd like to collaborate or get some help to get started. This is all (just) research and a trial to see what we can make, so nothing has to be perfect...^[...just hopefully better than what we've got so far - "A narrator with an Aussie accent? That's ridiculous! Try this instead" ]

Likewise, the website is hosted on Github (QR code in Figure 3^[Or at https://github.com/James-Reynolds/ROBUST_Electric_shaRed_mOBility_hUbS_Trial_website]), and uses open source software.  This means that you can edit it yourself and send me a 'pull request'. There are further details in the Readme of the github repository, or you can drop me an email or otherwise reach out if you'd like help getting started.

## Information - physical 

Thanks for the feedback on the research work done to date on developing Mobility Hub informational and directional signs. The software developed so far is available on github^[https://github.com/James-Reynolds/mobilityHubTools] as well as PDF versions of the Waterford totem / pedestal signs that we had printed out in A0 size at the workshop^[See *HERE* ] 



```{r plot_totems, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE, fig.fullwidth = TRUE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Waterford totems as per Bristol (left), Birmingham (centre) and a combined (right) style"}


knitr::include_graphics("graphics/Waterford_totem_1.png")

```


Note of course, that these a rough outlines and just what we have so far.  I'll be looking towards improving these based on your comments in the workshops^[Especially adding information about the topography!], and iterating improved designs. Please stay tuned for further details of what I come up with - perhaps we might be able to test some of them in the field and see what people on the street think?      


## More workshops? 

Noreen and I are off to Letterkenny and Galway over the next month or so to run workshops there.  But, neither of us is far away, and we'd certainly be interested in coming back to get your further thoughts an insights as the trial progresses and the iterative co-design processes iterate! 

More generally, I'm happy to come talk or otherwise interact about transport, implementation and policy-making, or pretty much any other related topic, so please let me know if that is of interest.  

All the best, 

James Reynolds^[email: james.reynolds@atu.ie]
